First, sendBeacon issues POST, while the server's removal route only accepts DELETE; unload therefore cannot retire sessions immediately. Add POST support to a dedicated presence/:session route or change beacon endpoint semantics. Second, concurrent save transactions can read current revision before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, creating a race. Node's single-threaded synchronous SQLite segment makes each save's synchronous validation+transaction uninterrupted after request body resolves, so two handlers do not interleave within that segment. Live revision events to the same saving client are ignored after its base updates because response JSON is sent before emit, although fetch continuation scheduling vs emit is worth noting: emit runs synchronously immediately after json and the browser handles separately; duplicate data either merges harmlessly or is ignored based on base.
